completed_tasks.name: Implement PageIndex schema and clinical reasoning tree generation
completed_tasks.notes: Decided against auto-generating trees from existing data sources: SFT medical dialogue data is Simplified Chinese TCM diagnosis Q&A (wrong language, wrong domain), and service_items payment_rules are generic coverage boilerplate with no clinical steps. Instead hand-wrote 4 more high-quality Traditional Chinese PageIndex trees (electrowave facelift, HA filler, fractional laser, HIFU lifting) alongside the existing 2 (laser resurfacing, botox), covering different anesthesia/downtime profiles as a quality baseline for TASK-004's LLM prompt. All 6 verified clean of price leakage and Simplified Chinese. Also found and fixed page_index_fts, which was still on unicode61 tokenizer from before the TASK-001 trigram migration — new trees were completely unsearchable until fixed; now all three FTS5 tables (drugs_fts, service_items_fts, page_index_fts) consistently use trigram.

completed_tasks.name: page_index_trees incremental update support + content versioning
completed_tasks.notes: Added content_version (increments on real content change), source_type (manual/llm_generated/clinic_upload), needs_regeneration (for future nightly batch to pick stale rows). seed_trees.py rewritten from INSERT OR REPLACE (wholesale overwrite, reset created_at every run) to true incremental UPSERT — compares existing content, skips if unchanged, updates + bumps content_version + preserves created_at if changed. Removed the duplicate create_sample_page_index() from scripts/seed_database.py (2 trees migrated into seed_trees.py's TREES list) so page_index_trees seeding has one single source of truth. Verified all three states (insert/skip-unchanged/update-with-version-bump) work correctly and FTS5 search still matches after updates. updated_at intentionally NOT trigger-maintained (avoids recursive UPDATE-trigger-updates-self risk) — application code must pass CURRENT_TIMESTAMP explicitly on updates.

Wrote .planning/VISION-EXPANSION.md (full gap analysis, decision log, phase 02-05 draft sequencing) and root-level Plan.md (single entry point for future LLM sessions) + AGENTS.md (binding project rules, modeled on DrtoolboxLocalServer's AGENTS.md).

completed_tasks.name: Build clinical reasoning tree LLM prompt
completed_tasks.notes: Built src/pageindex/prompt_template.py: build_prompt() assembles the generation prompt using 2 of the 6 hand-written trees as few-shot examples; generate_tree() takes a provider-agnostic llm_call: Callable[[str], str] so Phase 02's actual local-LLM client can be plugged in later without touching this code; parse_and_validate() enforces Traditional-Chinese-only, no price leakage, no overclaiming language (保證有效 etc.), all 5 required fields present, tolerates markdown code-fence-wrapped output. Also extracted the UPSERT logic that used to live only inside seed_trees.py into a new shared src/pageindex/db_writer.py (upsert_trees(conn, trees, source_type)) so both manual seeding and LLM generation write through the exact same incremental-upsert path — prevents repeating the TASK-003 mistake where seed_database.py and seed_trees.py each maintained a duplicate copy of the same 2 trees. Tested 7 validator scenarios (valid output, price leak, simplified Chinese, missing fields, overclaiming language, code-fence tolerance, malformed JSON) plus a full generate→validate→upsert→FTS5-search round trip against a scratch copy of clinic.db (not the real one). No real LLM available in this environment yet (no ollama/openai/anthropic client installed) — the prompt/validator were built and tested with a fake llm_call; actual model output quality is unverified until Phase 02 wires up a real local LLM.

completed_tasks.name: Implement search/query interface with routing
completed_tasks.notes: Built src/query/search.py (unified FTS5 trigram-vs-LIKE dispatch across drugs/service_items/page_index_trees, confirmed working correctly against page_index_trees despite its content_rowid='id' quirk) and src/query/router.py (classify() for special/general routing by keyword, mask_prices() as the final CONSTRAINT enforcement layer, handle_query() as the unified entry point). Found and fixed a real bug during testing: FTS5 trigram MATCH requires the whole query string to match contiguously, so passing a full natural-language question (e.g. '音波拉提會痛嗎？') straight to MATCH returns zero hits even though '音波拉提' exists in the data. Built extract_search_terms() to solve this — combines route-keyword hits with CJK-character-run extraction, split on common question-particle patterns (是什麼/多久/怎麼/etc.) as cut points, sorted longest-first to prioritize specificity, deduped. Verified against realistic full-sentence queries; the only remaining known imprecision is that generic 2-char words (e.g. 維持, appearing in most PageIndex summary_text values) can add noise to LIKE-fallback results, though longer/more-specific terms are tried first so the correct answer is usually still ranked first. general route currently returns zero page_index_trees hits for any query since all 6 seed trees are category='special' — this is expected, not a bug; general-category content doesn't exist until Phase 04's nightly batch generation produces some. No formal test file was added — TASK-008 (evaluation suite) is the designated place for building out regression tests covering the scenarios found here (full-sentence FTS failures, stopword-splitting, keyword-vs-CJK-fragment precision).

completed_tasks.name: Build OTC drug localization layer
completed_tasks.notes: First task in this project executed by an external tool (Antigravity) against a detailed written spec (.planning/phases/01-taiwan-pageindex-rag/TASK-006-PLAN.md), then independently re-verified by Claude before committing — not just trusting the delivery report. Added src/db/otc_mappings.json (68 ingredient mappings with alias support, replacing the 14-entry hardcoded dict in scripts/seed_database.py). update_otc_names() now reads the JSON; function signature and main() call site unchanged. src/query/search.py gained format_drug_display_name() + a display_name field auto-attached to search_drugs() results (verified it still passes through router.py's existing mask_prices() sweep, not bypassing it). src/query/router.py's stopword-split list gained common conjunctions (或/和/跟/有等) to handle compound colloquial questions like '請問有普拿疼或消炎止痛藥嗎？' — re-ran all 6 of TASK-005's prior test cases and got byte-identical results, no regression. Verified independently (re-ran everything myself, did not trust the delivery report's numbers as-is): coverage 456/7,573 (6.02%) → 2,484/7,573 (32.8%); full reseed completes in 1.7s with no errors; all 68 mapping entries clean of price leakage and Simplified Chinese; diff scope stayed within the 4 files the plan allowed. Found one inaccuracy in the delivery report worth flagging: it cited PARACETAMOL matching 3 records as proof the ACETAMINOPHEN/PARACETAMOL alias fix worked, but I verified there are zero drugs in this dataset that contain PARACETAMOL without also containing ACETAMINOPHEN — that specific case would have matched under the old logic too, alias or not. However I separately confirmed the alias mechanism itself is real and working: ASPIRIN/ACETYLSALICYLIC ACID recovered 1 additional record and MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE/MAGNESIUM OXIDE recovered 12, so the feature works, just the report's chosen example didn't actually demonstrate it.

completed_tasks.name: Integrate clinic database with RAG query
completed_tasks.notes: Second task executed by Antigravity against a written spec (.planning/phases/01-taiwan-pageindex-rag/TASK-007-PLAN.md), independently re-verified by Claude before commit. Added src/clinic/custom_notes.py: upsert_clinic_note() (true incremental UPSERT — same clinic_id+section always overwrites the single existing row, never appends; rejects invalid section or blank note with ValueError), get_clinic_custom_notes(), and 3 sample notes (pre_op/post_op_short/maintenance — deliberately skipped 'procedure' since a cross-procedure generic policy doesn't make sense for a section that's inherently procedure-specific; the delivery report didn't explain this omission, Claude inferred and accepted it as reasonable after checking). router.py gained get_clinic_custom_notes() wrapper + a clinic_custom_notes field on QueryResponse, populated only on the special route (never general — verified with 3+3 test queries, zero leakage), passed through the existing mask_prices() sweep. Claude independently re-ran everything rather than trusting the report: UPSERT dedup confirmed (2 writes to same clinic_id+section → still 1 row, second value wins), invalid-section and blank-note rejection confirmed, special/general isolation confirmed clean, full reseed pipeline still completes with no errors, all 6 of TASK-005's original test cases re-run byte-identical (no regression), no price leakage or Simplified Chinese in new content, diff scope stayed within the 2 files the plan allowed (plus the new src/clinic/ directory). One initial concern Claude raised (an apparent if/elif structure that looked like it could skip clinic_custom_notes when a query matched both clinic-ops and procedure keywords) turned out to be a misreading of the code on first pass — the clinic_info/clinic_hours fetch and the clinic_custom_notes fetch are two independent if-blocks, not a shared if/elif chain; confirmed non-issue by direct test. Also noted src/clinic/__init__.py breaks from every other module directory's convention of having no __init__.py, but confirmed via direct testing this doesn't affect imports (Python implicit namespace packages) — style inconsistency only, not a functional defect.

completed_tasks.name: Evaluation & testing suite
completed_tasks.notes: Third and final Phase 01 task executed by Antigravity against a written spec (.planning/phases/01-taiwan-pageindex-rag/TASK-008-PLAN.md), independently re-verified by Claude before commit — this is the project's first real test suite (91 pytest cases across tests/conftest.py + 5 test modules; everything before this was ad-hoc python3 -c one-liners re-typed manually each session). Covers: extract_search_terms() regression (the same 6 full-sentence cases manually re-verified across TASK-005/006/007, now locked in), mask_prices() format coverage, special/general route isolation (clinic_info/clinic_hours/clinic_custom_notes must be None/[]/{} on every general query — explicit assertions), OTC alias verification using the two CONFIRMED-working cases (ASPIRIN/ACETYLSALICYLIC ACID, MAGNESIUM HYDROXIDE/MAGNESIUM OXIDE) per the plan's explicit instruction to avoid the ACETAMINOPHEN/PARACETAMOL case shown in TASK-006 to not actually exercise the alias path, clinic_custom_notes UPSERT dedup (plus created_at preservation, beyond what the plan asked), invalid-input rejection, FTS5 trigram/LIKE boundary testing, and TASK-004's 7 validator scenarios formalized as the optional item. conftest.py isolates all DB access via shutil.copy2() — session-scope read-only copy, function-scope fresh copy per write test — never touches the real clinic.db directly. Claude independently re-verified rather than trusting the report: re-ran the full suite twice (91/91 passed both times), computed clinic.db's SHA-256 before and after test execution and confirmed byte-identical (05c0ac22...) — this was the single most important thing to check per the plan's own stated CONSTRAINT, and it held. Also independently queried the database to confirm the report's claimed '6 pure magnesium oxide + 6 aluminum-hydroxide compound' breakdown was accurate (it was), and confirmed clinic_custom_notes has no enforced FK constraint (SQLite foreign_keys pragma defaults off in this DB), so tests using nonexistent clinic_ids are valid, not accidentally-passing. Diff scope stayed clean — new tests/ directory only, zero changes to any existing src/ code, per the plan's CONSTRAINT against fixing bugs discovered during test-writing rather than just reporting them.

completed_tasks.name: Local LLM inference layer: llm_client adapter + political-stance guardrail + end-to-end generation
completed_tasks.notes: Executed by Antigravity against .planning/phases/02-local-llm-layer/TASK-PLAN.md, independently re-verified by Claude before commit (same delegation pattern as Phase 01 TASK-006/007/008). Added src/pageindex/llm_client.py: local_llm_call(prompt, timeout=90) calls the already-running llama-server (127.0.0.1:8080, Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL) via stdlib urllib only (no new dependency), does a GET /v1/models health check first, raises a custom LocalLLMUnavailableError with a clear Chinese message on connection failure/timeout instead of leaking a raw traceback or silently returning empty output, and strictly extracts only message.content (discards the model's non-standard reasoning_content field). Function signature matches generate_tree()'s expected Callable[[str], str] exactly, so it plugs in with no wrapper. prompt_template.py gained a 7th strict rule (existing rules 1-6 left untouched) prohibiting political/sovereignty/ideological stance content, plus a new _POLITICAL_STANCE_PHRASES tuple + check in parse_and_validate() modeled on the existing _FORBIDDEN_PHRASES mechanism — raises TreeValidationError with a distinct message (not conflated with the price/simplified-Chinese/overclaiming checks) so violations are easy to categorize. This guardrail exists because real-machine testing found the local Qwen model outputs PRC-official-line content on politically sensitive prompts (e.g. Taiwan sovereignty questions); user's explicit decision was to keep using this existing service as-is (no redeploy, no model swap) and defend via prompt+validator layers instead. Claude independently re-verified rather than trusting the delivery report: personally ran llm_client.py against the live server and confirmed real content came back; personally constructed a political-stance test string and confirmed parse_and_validate() correctly raises TreeValidationError; re-ran pytest tests/ and got 100/100 passing (91 prior + 9 new in tests/test_llm_client.py and tests/test_prompt_template.py); computed clinic.db SHA-256 before/after and confirmed byte-identical — zero pollution of the real database; personally inspected the 3 real LLM-generated trees (淨膚雷射/水飛梭/自體脂肪補臉, all new procedures not overlapping the 6 hand-written seed trees) written only to an isolated test-copy database via db_writer.upsert_trees(source_type='llm_generated'), confirmed reasonable content and full validator pass. Cloud API fallback was explicitly out of scope (interface-only, not implemented). Known caveat carried into future phases: the _POLITICAL_STANCE_PHRASES list is an initial sample, not exhaustive — documented as needing expansion if real-world generation surfaces new stance phrasings the current list misses.

blockers.description: extract_search_terms() is a simple keyword/CJK-run heuristic, not real Chinese word segmentation. Generic 2-char terms (e.g. 維持, 回診) can appear in most page_index_trees rows, adding noise to LIKE-fallback results in the middle of a result set (correct answer is usually still ranked first due to longer-term priority, but not guaranteed). This is now covered by regression tests but not eliminated as a limitation.
blockers.workaround: Evaluate a real Chinese tokenizer (e.g. jieba) if real-world usage in Phase 04 shows this degrades result quality in practice

decisions.decision: Use dual-layer architecture: General NHI data + Clinic-specific data
decisions.rationale: Separates concerns and allows independent updates

decisions.decision: Implement route-based context gathering (special vs general)
decisions.rationale: Prevents information overload and ensures clinic-specific data doesn't leak

decisions.decision: Absolute price masking rule for all outputs
decisions.rationale: Taiwan medical compliance prohibits any price information in AI outputs

decisions.decision: Exclusive use of繁體中文 in all outputs

decisions.rationale: Reliability with future expansion capability from NHI database

decisions.decision: Local LLM inference is the default, cloud API is fallback-only
decisions.rationale: Matches prior project DrtoolboxLocalServer's privacy-first, zero-cloud-dependency principle; user explicitly confirmed this preference

decisions.decision: Nightly batch job does both: (1) pre-generate common Q&A pairs via LLM into a cache table, (2) maintain/rebuild PageIndex trees and re-index new documents
decisions.rationale: User confirmed both are needed — reduces daytime LLM token cost by serving cached answers first, while keeping the knowledge base current

decisions.decision: page_index_trees must support incremental updates going forward (content_version, source_type, needs_regeneration), not wholesale INSERT OR REPLACE
decisions.rationale: User explicitly asked to prioritize this — an updatable database design is a prerequisite for reducing future token usage (query DB first, only call LLM for what's missing/stale)

decisions.decision: doctor-toolbox.com integration will use their official API for bidirectional import/export, not the prior project's MITM interception approach
decisions.rationale: User explicitly rejected the MITM pattern when asked to clarify; wants a proper API contract instead. Scheduled after clinicbrain's own phases (01-04) are complete.

decisions.decision: Keep using the existing local Qwen3.8-27B llama-server as-is (no redeploy, no model swap) despite it outputting PRC-official-line content on politically sensitive prompts; defend via a prompt-layer rule (7th strict rule) plus a validator-layer keyword check (_POLITICAL_STANCE_PHRASES) instead
decisions.rationale: User explicitly confirmed continuing with the existing service; re-deploying/swapping models was considered out of proportion to the risk, since the prompt+validator double-defense fits the project's existing CONSTRAINT-enforcement architecture pattern (same mechanism already used for price leakage and Simplified Chinese detection)

decisions.decision: Clinic business documents (緻妍外科診所/) get converted to Q&A pairs via LLM before entering the knowledge base, not directly into page_index_trees' four-section structure; the FAQ cache table design must be shared with the nightly-batch common-Q&A pre-generation mechanism (not a separate schema)
decisions.rationale: User confirmed both document-derived and general-knowledge-derived FAQ content should share one table design rather than maintaining two parallel schemas for the same conceptual thing

decisions.decision: New standalone faq_cache table (not merged into page_index_trees): clinic_id, topic_key (nullable, NULL=general), question, answer, category, source_type/content_version/needs_regeneration mirroring page_index_trees' field semantics exactly, plus faq_cache_fts (trigram)
decisions.rationale: Q&A is a flat one-question-one-answer shape, structurally different from page_index_trees' four-section clinical reasoning tree — forcing both into one table would make the query layer guess which shape a row is. Reusing the same content_version/source_type/needs_regeneration semantics (not the same table) lets the future nightly-batch maintenance job use one 'find needs_regeneration=1 rows' pattern across both tables without a separate mechanism.

decisions.decision: page_index_trees gets a real clinic_id column (FK to clinic_info); doc_id becomes a clinic-prefix-free procedure slug (e.g. zhiyan-clinic-hifu-lifting → hifu-lifting)
decisions.rationale: Discovered during 2026-09-22 planning session that page_index_trees currently has NO clinic_id column at all — clinic identity lives only as a string prefix on doc_id, parsed via hardcoded string matching in prompt_template.py (_FEW_SHOT_DOC_IDS, .replace('zhiyan-clinic-', '')). This is technical debt, not a design choice worth preserving. A real column lets 'all trees for this clinic' be a plain WHERE clinic_id = ? query instead of LIKE 'prefix-%', and means doc_id never needs a second rewrite if the clinic_id naming scheme changes again later (e.g. once Phase 05's doctor-toolbox.com integration is real).
